role: Saudi Aramco's main crude export terminal
roleNotes: Saudi Aramco's Gulf-coast export complex: Eastern Province crude loads at the Sea Islands and the six-buoy Juaymah SPM terminal, refined products ship from the North Pier and the adjoining 550,000 b/d refinery, and refrigerated LPG loads at the Juaymah LPG pier; every cargo sails out through the Strait of Hormuz.

terminals.name: Ras Tanura Terminal, North Pier (berths 6 to 11)

role: Red Sea outlet of the East-West pipeline, Hormuz bypass
roleNotes: Red Sea terminus of Saudi Aramco's East-West crude pipeline: crude loads at the four-berth North Crude Terminal and the three-berth South Terminal, and refined products from the Aramco Yanbu, SAMREF and YASREF refineries ship from adjacent product berths, giving Saudi exports a route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.

terminals.name: Yanbu North Refined Product Terminal (berths 91 to 94)
YASREF sulphur, oil and petroleum coke terminal and NGL berth

role: Gulf of Oman storage and bunkering hub outside Hormuz
roleNotes: Gulf of Oman terminus of ADNOC's Habshan-Fujairah crude pipeline (ADCOP, about 1.8 million b/d of transmission capacity), which lets Abu Dhabi crude load outside the Strait of Hormuz, with the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone tank farms feeding the FOTT berths and the world's second largest bunkering hub.

terminals.name: Fujairah Oil Tanker Terminals (FOTT) berths and VLCC jetty
ADNOC Fujairah crude oil export terminal (ADCOP terminus)
terminals.operator: ADNOC (Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline LLC)

terminals.name: Former Brooge Energy storage and blending terminal

role: Largest LNG export complex
roleNotes: Owned, regulated and operated by QatarEnergy, the loading point for QatarEnergy LNG's 14 trains (77 mtpa) across six Q-Flex and Q-Max capable LNG berths, plus condensate, LPG, sulphur, Laffan Refinery products and the Pearl and Oryx GTL liquids, every seaborne cargo of which transits the Strait of Hormuz.

terminals.name: Ras Laffan LNG berths (six berths, 14 trains)
Ras Laffan Terminal Operations (condensate, LPG, sulphur, GTL berths)
Ras Laffan Petrochemicals ethane cracker (start-up expected late 2026)

role: Sanctioned crude export terminal
roleNotes: Iran's principal crude and condensate export terminal, loading about nine tenths of the country's oil exports from a 32 to 34 million barrel tank farm fed by pipelines from the Gachsaran, Ahvaz and Marun fields, through the eastern T-Jetty and the western Sea Island (Azarpad) ULCC berths, 660 km northwest of the Strait of Hormuz.

authority.name: Iranian Oil Terminals Company (IOTC, National Iranian Oil Company)

terminals.name: T-Jetty (eastern oil loading jetty, VLCC berths)
Sea Island / Azarpad jetty (western ULCC berths)
Kharg Chemical Complex (KHEMCO) sulphur and LPG berth
Kharg crude and products tank farm

role: Largest US crude export and petrochemical complex
roleNotes: The 52-mile Houston Ship Channel hosts Enterprise's LPG and ethane export docks at Morgan's Point, the Kinder Morgan and ONEOK refined-product hubs at Pasadena and Galena Park, the ExxonMobil Baytown and Pemex Deer Park refineries and the US Gulf Coast's main residual-fuel and bunkering market, and is one of the two largest US crude export points.

terminals.name: Enterprise Hydrocarbons Terminal and Morgan's Point ethane export terminal
Kinder Morgan Pasadena and Galena Park terminals (with BOSTCO)
Energy Transfer Houston Terminal (former HFOTCO), Jacintoport
ExxonMobil Baytown refinery and chemical complex docks

role: Largest US crude export port, LNG
roleNotes: The largest US crude export gateway, loading Permian and Eagle Ford crude onto VLCCs at the Ingleside terminals (Enbridge and Gibson South Texas Gateway) and Inner Harbor docks, while Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction plant on the La Quinta Channel exports LNG and the Valero and Citgo refineries take crude in and ship products out across the ship channel.

terminals.name: Corpus Christi Crude terminal (former NuStar North Beach)

role: First and largest US LNG export terminal
roleNotes: Cheniere's six-train, roughly 30 mtpa Sabine Pass Liquefaction plant on the Louisiana bank of the pass, in service since 2016, loads LNG carriers at three berths from interstate and intrastate pipeline gas, and since 2026 shares the pass with the QatarEnergy and ExxonMobil Golden Pass export terminal on the Texas bank.

terminals.name: Sabine Pass LNG terminal (six trains, three berths)
Sabine Pass Stage 5 expansion (Train 7, about 6 mtpa, pre-FID)
terminals.operator: Cheniere Energy (Sabine Pass Liquefaction Stage V)

terminals.name: Golden Pass LNG (Texas bank, three trains, first cargo April 2026)
terminals.operator: Golden Pass LNG (QatarEnergy and ExxonMobil affiliates)

role: Gulf refining (Motiva), Sabine-Neches waterway
roleNotes: On the Sabine-Neches Waterway 19 miles from the Gulf, hosting three crude-fed refineries with their own docks (Motiva's 730,000 b/d plant, North America's largest, plus Valero and TotalEnergies), Energy Transfer's Nederland crude and NGL export terminal upstream on the Neches, and Sempra's Port Arthur LNG under construction.

authority.name: Port of Port Arthur Navigation District

terminals.name: Motiva Port Arthur refinery docks (730,000 b/d)
Valero Port Arthur refinery docks (435,000 b/d)
TotalEnergies Port Arthur refinery docks (238,000 b/d)
Nederland Terminal (six ship docks, crude and NGL)

role: Europe's crude and product hub (ARA), Gate LNG
roleNotes: Europe's largest crude import and product trading hub: the Maasvlakte and Europoort crude terminals feed the Pernis and Europoort refineries and the pipelines into Germany and Belgium, the Botlek and Europoort tank farms anchor the ARA product market, and Gate terminal is the Dutch LNG import point.

role: ARA refining and chemicals
roleNotes: Second leg of the ARA hub on the Scheldt: the TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil refineries and Europe's largest integrated chemical cluster take crude and feedstock over the port's jetties, while the Evos, Sea-Tank and ATPC tank farms trade refined products with Rotterdam and Amsterdam by barge and pipeline.

role: ARA gasoline and product storage
roleNotes: The gasoline leg of the ARA hub: the Westpoort tank farms behind the IJmuiden sea locks blend and store gasoline, diesel and jet for the Atlantic Basin export trade, and the port is one of the largest petrol ports in the world by throughput.

role: UK LNG (South Hook, Dragon) and refining
roleNotes: Deep-water natural harbour in Pembrokeshire that lands most of the United Kingdom's LNG at the South Hook and Dragon terminals and hosts the Valero Pembroke refinery, making it the UK's largest energy port by tonnage.

terminals.name: Puma Energy Milford Haven terminal (former Murco refinery)

role: Black Sea crude and CPC terminal
roleNotes: Russia's main Black Sea crude and products outlet: the Sheskharis terminal loads Urals crude and products from the Transneft system, and the Caspian Pipeline Consortium marine terminal at Yuzhnaya Ozereyevka loads Kazakh CPC Blend from single-point moorings, all sailing through the Bosporus.

role: Baltic crude outlet
roleNotes: End point of the Baltic Pipeline System on the Gulf of Finland and Russia's largest Baltic oil-loading port: Transneft loads Urals crude at the oil terminal and diesel from the Sever products pipeline at the products berths, with cargoes sailing out past the Danish straits.

role: Bunkering, refining and trading hub
roleNotes: The world's largest bunkering port and Asia's oil trading and pricing hub: the Jurong Island and Pulau Bukom refineries and the island tank farms sit on the Malacca and Singapore Straits route between Middle East crude and North-East Asian demand, and the Singapore LNG terminal supplies the city's gas.

authority.name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

terminals.name: Pulau Bukom refinery and terminal
terminals.operator: Aster Chemicals and Energy (former Shell Bukom)

role: China's crude gateway (Ningbo-Zhoushan)
roleNotes: The world's busiest port by tonnage and China's largest crude import gateway: VLCC berths at Daxie, Zhenhai and the Zhoushan islands feed the Sinopec Zhenhai refinery, the Zhoushan commercial and strategic crude reserves and the Yangtze delta refining belt, and the Zhoushan and Ningbo LNG terminals receive gas.

terminals.name: Zhenhai Refining and Chemical crude berths
Zhoushan (Aoshan) crude oil storage and berths
terminals.operator: Sinopec Zhoushan and the national reserve

role: SK Energy and S-Oil refining complex
roleNotes: South Korea's largest liquid-bulk port: the SK Energy Ulsan complex and the S-Oil Onsan refinery take Middle East crude over their own berths and ship products and petrochemicals back out, alongside the Korea National Oil Corporation stockpile and the Korea Oil Terminal tank farms, on the Korea Strait route.

terminals.name: Korea National Oil Corporation Ulsan stockpile base

role: Tokyo Bay refining
roleNotes: Japan's largest port by tonnage, spanning the Keiyo industrial belt on the east shore of Tokyo Bay: the Idemitsu and Cosmo Chiba refineries, the Fuji Oil Sodegaura refinery and the shared Keiyo Sea Berth VLCC crude terminal, with the Sodegaura LNG terminal feeding the Tokyo gas and power market.

terminals.name: Keiyo Sea Berth (shared VLCC crude berth)
terminals.operator: Keiyo Sea Berth Co. (Idemitsu, Cosmo and Fuji Oil)

role: Outlet of the Jamnagar refinery (Reliance)
roleNotes: Captive marine terminal of the Reliance Jamnagar complex, the world's largest refinery site: single-point moorings off Sikka receive crude that has crossed the Arabian Sea from the Gulf, and the product jetties ship diesel, gasoline and jet to Europe, Asia and Africa.

terminals.name: Reliance Jamnagar SPM crude terminals off Sikka
Reliance Sikka marine terminal product jetties
Jamnagar refinery complex (DTA and SEZ refineries)
